provenance_envelope.reason: The authentication gate request GET https://api.github.com/rate_limit was issued before harvesting - its observed values are carried in _capture.rate_limit_observed and described in _capture.notes - but its per-call record was never written into _capture.calls. This artifact therefore cannot audit that one request's HTTP status or record count. The harvested records themselves are unaffected and remain COMPLETE.

unrecorded_requests.provenance: UNKNOWN AS RECORDED - the limit/remaining/reset triple in _capture.rate_limit_observed cannot be observed without issuing this request, so the request was issued; but no field of this artifact RECORDS its HTTP status or its record count, so both are carried here as the literal string UNKNOWN, and on the itemized _capture.calls[0] entry both are null and named in its unknown_fields. INFERENCE - the request nonetheless succeeded, because _capture.notes records that resources.core.limit = 5000 was read from the response BODY, a body shape this endpoint returns only on success; the reasoning is recorded at _capture.calls[0].record_provenance and is deliberately not written into the status field, which carries observations only. UNKNOWN - the record count is genuinely unrecoverable: no value for it is entailed by anything preserved here, and none was manufactured.

provenance_envelope.recovery_action_refused: Re-issuing the request to manufacture a call record is forbidden: the upstream repository is archived and this capture is one-time and non-repeatable, so a request issued now would carry a different timestamp and a different remaining count and would not be the record that is missing. Fabricating the two values is likewise refused. The omission is reported instead.

calls.record_provenance: RECONSTRUCTED_FROM_PRESERVED_EVIDENCE - this entry was not written into calls[] at capture time and was reconstructed afterwards from evidence preserved inside this same artifact, without re-issuing the request. url and method: named verbatim in _capture.notes as the endpoint the authentication gate probed by GET. x_ratelimit_limit / x_ratelimit_remaining / x_ratelimit_reset: taken from _capture.rate_limit_observed, which _capture.notes records as the reading observed at that gate call. http_status: left null and named in unknown_fields, because no field of this artifact records it. INFERENCE - the request nonetheless succeeded, since _capture.notes records that resources.core.limit = 5000 was read from the response BODY and corroborated the x-ratelimit-limit header, a body shape this endpoint returns only on success; that is an inference and is deliberately not written into the http_status field, which carries observations only. link_next null: this endpoint is not paginated.
unrecoverable_fields: records_returned - genuinely not recorded anywhere in this artifact and deliberately left null rather than inferred; sibling captures 53.json and 220.json record null for this same endpoint while 323.json records 1, so no single value is entailed

record_counts.per_call_provenance: PARTIAL - 3 of 3 issued requests are itemised in calls[], but calls[0] is reconstructed from preserved in-artifact evidence rather than recorded at capture time, and its records_returned is unrecoverable. Thread content is complete and reconciled; per-request provenance is not.

notes: FACT - Environment activation: /etc/profile.d/blitzy-cobolcheck-env.sh was present in this container and was sourced as the first command of the session. This capture needs nothing beyond python3 and curl, both already on PATH, so no dependent value in this file is unestablished on its account.

FACT - Tooling was observed in this container rather than assumed and nothing was installed; the observed values are recorded in _capture.tooling. The capture was driven entirely by python3 urllib.request so that response headers could be read separately from response bodies, with no possibility of headers being spliced into a body.

FACT - The `authenticated` field was derived solely from the observed rate-limit ceiling returned by GET https://api.github.com/rate_limit: the x-ratelimit-limit response header read 5000 and was corroborated by resources.core.limit = 5000 in the response body. The unauthenticated control ceiling is 60 and was not observed. The presence of a token variable in the environment was never used as the basis for this field, because an exhausted unauthenticated quota returns empty response bodies rather than errors and would corrupt this capture silently instead of failing loudly.

FACT - The gate reading and the per-call readings differ, and both are recorded verbatim as observed rather than reconciled: _capture.rate_limit_observed holds remaining = 5000 with reset = 1786688052 as observed at the authentication gate, while each _capture.calls[] entry holds the value observed at that call's own instant - x_ratelimit_remaining 4965 then 4964, with reset 1786684750 on every call.

UNKNOWN - What consumed the gap between the gate reading and the first capture call is not established by anything this capture retained. FACT - across the capture the remaining values decrease by exactly one per request issued here, which accounts for this capture's own consumption in full and places the remainder of the gap outside this capture; GET https://api.github.com/rate_limit does not itself count against the core quota. FACT - the ceiling stayed at 5000 on every call, so the authentication determination is unaffected.

FACT - Comment pagination followed the Link rel="next" header to exhaustion rather than assuming a single page: rel="next" was absent from the first response, so the chain terminated with link_next = null on every recorded call after 1 page, returning 4 comment records in total.

FACT - Completeness cross-check passed: the assembled issue_comments array holds 4 records and the GET https://api.github.com/repos/openmainframeproject/cobol-check/issues/321 payload independently reports comments = 4. The two counts agree, so no silent truncation occurred and no discrepancy entry is warranted.

FACT - The issue's updated_at (2026-01-14T19:47:18Z) is identical to the created_at of the newest captured comment (id 3751338621), so the thread's own newest record is what sets the issue's updated_at. The preceding comments are dated 2023-11-13T14:16:37Z, 2023-11-13T14:44:30Z, 2024-02-01T20:22:52Z. Nothing observed here contradicts the carried-forward characterization of #321 as an issue with recent activity.

UNKNOWN - Whether issue #321 is the *only* upstream issue with recent activity could not be established from within this capture, because that is a comparison across all upstream open issues and no cross-issue listing was read here. Both the comparison and its verdict belong to upstream-harvest/HARVEST-MANIFEST.md, so no ranking is asserted in this file.

FACT - Every HTTP request recorded in _capture.calls[] is a GET. No write of any kind - no comment, reaction, label, assignment, reopen or edit - was attempted against the archived upstream repository openmainframeproject/cobol-check.

FACT - Comment and issue payloads are stored exactly as returned: no field was pruned and no body was truncated, reflowed, re-rendered from markdown, HTML-stripped or whitespace-normalized. Each comment retains all 14 fields GitHub returned and the issue payload retains all 34, in GitHub's own field order. The issue body contains CRLF sequences; JSON string escaping represents each as the two-character escape \r\n, so the serialized file holds no raw carriage-return byte while every value still round-trips byte-identically.

FACT: CREDENTIAL TRANSPORT — the HTTP client recorded for this artifact is python3 `urllib.request` at `_capture.tooling.capture_driver`, which runs in process: the credential was read from the environment and set as a request header inside the capture process, so it entered no process argument vector. The classification is machine-readable at `_capture.credential_transport_exposure = "in_process_client_only"`. No credential value, header or fragment appears anywhere in this artifact at rest, and every call in `_capture.calls` is a `GET`. The transport rule binding any future authenticated capture is fixed in `upstream-harvest/HARVEST-MANIFEST.md` section 3.3.1.

FACT: PUBLIC-DATA GOVERNANCE — this artifact retains public GitHub records verbatim, including contributor `login`, profile and avatar URLs, timestamps and comment bodies, because it is the audit copy of a one-time capture against an archived repository and fidelity is its purpose. Use of that data is bounded to backlog triage and provenance audit for this programme. The binding purpose, access and publication boundary, retention trigger, disposal rule, deleted-upstream-content handling and the prohibition on profiling, enrichment, outreach and every other secondary use are stated in `upstream-harvest/HARVEST-MANIFEST.md` section 12. Those rules constrain use and lifetime; they never license editing this evidence.

issue.title: FR: please co-publish vscode extension on Open VSX Registry
issue.body:
Please add this useful extension to the [Open VSX Registry](https://open-vsx.org/?search=cobol).

Details on the publishing can be found at https://github.com/eclipse/openvsx/wiki/Publishing-Extensions.

A bit of explanation:
Open VSX Registry is the default extension provider endpoint for the free build of vscode VSCodium and Eclipse Theia, as well as browser versions like the one on GitPod. It would be nice to have this extension be directly published to a free vsix repository instead of only the Microsoft Marketplace with its restrictions.

You could also use a [GitHub action](https://docs.github.com/en/actions) that allows publishing to Open VSX and the MS market place, [HaaLeo/publish-vscode-extension](https://github.com/HaaLeo/publish-vscode-extension#readme) does this.
